import torch
import torch.nn as nn

COL = 64
WIDTH = 48
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + COL, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * (WIDTH + COL), 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        c = self.col(obs)
        f = torch.cat([self.body(c), c], dim=1)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

W = 32
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.nt = spec.n_types
        c_l = 14
        self.ctx = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 1)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(c_l, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.score = nn.Conv2d(W, 2 * spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        b = obs[:, 0:Z]
        t = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        m = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        e = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        g = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3]
        cur = torch.stack([b, t, m, e], dim=2)
        nb = torch.stack([b, t, m], dim=2)
        zero = torch.zeros_like(nb[:, :1])
        below = torch.cat([zero, nb[:, :-1]], dim=1)
        above = torch.cat([nb[:, 1:], zero], dim=1)
        gl = g.unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, 3, Y, X)
        zc = (torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / Z).view(1, Z, 1, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, 1, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([cur, below, above, gl, zc], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 14, Y, X)
        ctx = self.ctx(obs)
        h = self.conv1(x).view(B, Z, W, Y, X) + ctx.unsqueeze(1)
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, W, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.conv2(h))
        s = self.score(h).view(B, Z, 2, self.nt, Y, X)
        w = torch.softmax(s[:, :, 0], dim=1)
        place = (w * s[:, :, 1]).sum(1).flatten(1)
        h5 = h.view(B, Z, W, Y, X)
        c = F.relu(ctx)
        pooled = torch.cat([h5.mean((1, 3, 4)), h5.amax((1, 3, 4)), c.mean((2, 3)), c.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gf = self.glob(pooled)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gf)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gf).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

COL = 64
WIDTH = 48
HEADS = 4
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3}


class Attn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d, h):
        super().__init__()
        self.h = h
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d, 3 * d)
        self.out = nn.Linear(d, d)

    def forward(self, x):
        B, N, D = x.shape
        dh = D // self.h
        y = self.norm(x)
        q, k, v = self.qkv(y).chunk(3, dim=-1)
        q = q.reshape(B, N, self.h, dh).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.reshape(B, N, self.h, dh).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.reshape(B, N, self.h, dh).transpose(1, 2)
        att = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(dh), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(att, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, D)
        return x + self.out(o)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.attn = Attn(WIDTH, HEADS)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + COL, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * (WIDTH + COL), 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        c = self.col(obs)
        b = self.body(c)
        t = b.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        t = self.attn(t)
        b = t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, WIDTH, Y, X)
        f = torch.cat([b, c], dim=1)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

COL = 64
WIDTH = 48
P = 32
H = 32
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 2}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.my = max(fp[0] for fp in self.fps) - 1
        self.mx = max(fp[1] for fp in self.fps) - 1
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + COL, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + COL, P, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_mlp = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * P, H, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(H, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * (WIDTH + COL), 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        c = self.col(obs)
        f = torch.cat([self.body(c), c], dim=1)
        p = self.proj(f)
        pp = F.pad(p, (0, self.mx, 0, self.my))
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            sh = [pp[:, :, i:i + Y, j:j + X] for i in range(dy) for j in range(dx)]
            st = torch.stack(sh, 0)
            a = torch.cat([st.amax(0), st.mean(0)], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_mlp[t](a))
        place = (self.place_head(f) + torch.cat(outs, dim=1)).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.mx = max(fp[1] for fp in self.fps) - 1
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + COL, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(WIDTH + COL, P, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.type_mlp = nn.ModuleList([
            nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * P, H, 1), nn.ReLU(), nn.Conv2d(H, 1, 1))
            for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * (WIDTH + COL), 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        c = self.col(obs)
        f = torch.cat([self.body(c), c], dim=1)
        p = self.proj(f)
        pp = F.pad(p, (0, self.mx, 0, self.my))
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            sh = [pp[:, :, i:i + Y, j:j + X] for i in range(dy) for j in range(dx)]
            st = torch.stack(sh, 0)
            a = torch.cat([st.amax(0), st.mean(0)], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_mlp[t](a))
        place = (self.place_head(f) + torch.cat(outs, dim=1)).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting architecture's 4 seeds (0.068, 0.068, 0.258, 0.068) suggest each run either learns to finish exact builds or stalls near 0.07, so a 2-seed mean can move by about 0.1 from luck alone. The default recipe gives only about 32 PPO updates of 4,096 samples, which is very few improvement steps. The decision that matters is per anchor: where does the brick land (the highest filled cell under its footprint), and are the target cells at that layer missing over the whole footprint, with nothing missing below them? That combines a spatial max with a per-layer match, which a shallow 2D conv over stacked layer channels may learn slowly. All three candidates share one recipe: 128 envs, ppo_epochs 3, 16 minibatches. That gives about 83 smaller updates at r=1. Candidate 1 isolates the recipe; candidates 2 and 3 change the network on top of it.
analyses.2: 0.068 looks like a floor: a policy stuck in a poor local optimum gives exactly this score. The starting net hit it in 3 of 4 seeds. r1c1 (recipe only) and r1c3 (per-layer landing attention) both stayed at the floor. r1c2 (per-column 1x1 MLP before the 3x3 convs) is the only trial to escape it: 0.109 and 0.400. That fits the idea that learning per-column vertical summaries (height, the target pattern above it) is the hard part. Seed variance is huge, so r1c2 needs refinements that make escape more reliable. Train success (0.246) is close to dev, so the agent is undertrained and not overfitting. This round: (A) the same r1c2 network with fewer PPO epochs, giving about 45% more samples; (B) per-anchor reasoning made deeper with 1x1 layers after a single footprint gather; (C) a new idea, global self-attention over cells for ordering and context, built on r1c2.
analyses.3: Results are bimodal. Seeds either stay at the 0.068 floor, which is probably a collapsed degenerate policy, or escape to 0.4–0.55. Only the column-MLP family has ever escaped: r1c2, r2c1 and r2c2 each have one strong seed. All three have one weak seed (two near 0.11, one at the floor), so their means differ by less than the seed noise. Two things hurt: global attention (r2c3) and the per-layer landing design (r1c3). Both added compute and both stayed on the floor in every seed. Fewer epochs with more fresh samples (r2c1) gave the best single seed, which fits an agent that is short of data. The main problem now is how reliably a seed escapes the floor, not peak capacity. This round tests: (1) pushing samples further with 1 epoch; (2) r2c2's anchor MLP combined with 2 epochs; (3) a more uniform starting policy, using a small-init policy head and a higher entropy coefficient, to stop early collapse.
analyses.4: Every failed seed, whatever the architecture, scores exactly 0.0684 (35/512). That points to one shared local optimum. My guess, which these results cannot confirm, is that the agent learns to fill target cells that have no overhang and never learns when to place a wide brick across a gap. The column-MLP-first design (r1c2/r2c1) is the only clear architectural gain: three of its four seeds escaped the floor and reached 0.40–0.55. Two PPO epochs (about 213k steps) beat three. One epoch (373k steps) fell to the floor, so the number of optimisation steps matters as well as the number of samples. Both runs with a compute ratio of about 1.5 (attention, per-layer conv) hit the floor. A near-uniform starting policy with more entropy did not stop collapse. Untested so far: discounting. With gamma 0.95, the +1 exact-build bonus is heavily discounted, which favours greedy, safe fills over choosing the right order for overhangs. Also untested: a placement head aligned exactly to each brick footprint, so the network can find the landing layer.
